root.summary: As of the end of 2024, IonQ is advancing quantum computing through scalable modular architectures, achieving significant milestones like AQ35 early and shifting focus to photonic interconnects. The company emphasizes trapped ion qubits with all-to-all connectivity and is innovating in quantum error correction to enhance qubit fidelity and stability. Strategic priorities include expanding engineering capacity, supporting multi-year simulation roadmaps, and promoting Quantum Computing as a Service to broaden ecosystem engagement. IonQ is also addressing key quantum networking challenges and exploring quantum algorithms with societal impact in logistics, pharmaceuticals, and climate modeling. Overall, IonQ is positioning itself to overcome technical barriers while expanding market reach and technological capabilities.
shifts: 2020: Introduced Algorithmic Qubits and planned modular quantum computers networked by 2023.
2023: Expanded modular architectures via acquisitions and multi-QPU protocols; achieved AQ25 milestone.
2024: Achieved AQ35 target early; shifted focus to photonic interconnects and all-optical switching.
2024: Emphasized trapped ion qubits with scalability and all-to-all connectivity at room temperature.
2024: Strategic focus on expanding engineering capacity and supporting multi-year simulation roadmaps.
2024: Promoted Quantum Computing as a Service to accelerate adoption and ecosystem growth.

glossary.name: Algorithmic Qubits
glossary.definition: The largest number of effectively perfect qubits you can deploy for a typical quantum program.

glossary.name: Barium Ions
glossary.definition: Ions specifically selected for quantum computing that emit visible light, simplifying photon collection and transmission for quantum networking.

glossary.name: IonQ Forte
glossary.definition: IonQ's flagship, commercially available quantum computer designed to push the boundaries of performance through hardware and software upgrades.

glossary.name: Physical Qubit Count
glossary.definition: The total number of physical qubits present in a quantum computer.

glossary.name: Quantum Networking
glossary.definition: Technology that connects multiple quantum processing units to create a stronger, shared quantum computing system by exchanging quantum information, often using photons.

glossary.name: AWS Amazon Braket
glossary.definition: Amazon Web Services' cloud platform providing access to quantum computers including IonQ's systems.

glossary.name: Acousto-Optic Deflectors
glossary.definition: Devices that enable the precise steering of control lasers to dynamically address ions at different locations in the quantum processor.

glossary.name: All-to-All Connectivity
glossary.definition: A system architecture where each qubit can directly interact with any other qubit in the system, enhancing computational power and reducing circuit complexity.

glossary.name: Amplitude Estimation Circuits
glossary.definition: A family of benchmark circuits used in the #AQ repository to evaluate quantum computer performance.

glossary.name: Application-Based Benchmarking
glossary.definition: A benchmarking approach that rewards improvements across the entire quantum computing stack by evaluating performance on representative commercial algorithmic approaches.

glossary.name: Aria
glossary.definition: IonQ's industry-leading quantum computing system that achieved the #AQ25 milestone, demonstrating state-of-the-art quantum computational power.

glossary.name: Battery-Chemistry Simulation
glossary.definition: Simulations focused on next-generation solid-state battery chemistries to support materials science research.

glossary.name: Circuit Depth Tolerance
glossary.definition: The maximum allowable depth of quantum circuits that a system can execute effectively.

glossary.name: Cloud Execution
glossary.definition: Running quantum workloads on cloud platforms such as AWS Braket to enable remote access to quantum computing resources.

glossary.name: Coherence Time
glossary.definition: The duration for which a qubit maintains its quantum state before decoherence occurs, critical for performing quantum computations.

glossary.name: Compiler Optimization
glossary.definition: Techniques applied to quantum circuit compilation to reduce two-qubit gate counts and improve performance on benchmark circuits.

glossary.name: Detection Optics
glossary.definition: Optical components designed and installed to accurately image and measure longer qubit chains in the quantum processor.

glossary.name: Drug Discovery
glossary.definition: The use of quantum computing to improve the speed and accuracy of virtual screening and molecular docking predictions to reduce drug development costs and time to market.

glossary.name: Entangled Networks
glossary.definition: A company acquired by IonQ to aid in developing modular architecture and tools for distributing workloads across quantum processing units.

glossary.name: Entanglement Generation Rate
aliases: rate of information exchange between QPUs
glossary.definition: The speed at which quantum entanglement is generated between quantum processing units, affecting the scalability of quantum computation.

glossary.name: Error Mitigation
glossary.definition: Techniques used to reduce the impact of errors in quantum computations without full error correction.

glossary.name: Error-Corrected Qubit Ratio
glossary.definition: The ratio of physical qubits required to form a single error-corrected qubit, varying by quantum architecture.

glossary.name: Error-Mitigation Strategies
glossary.definition: Techniques used to reduce the impact of errors in quantum computations without full error correction.

glossary.name: Fault Tolerant Error Corrected Operation
glossary.definition: An operation on a quantum computer that uses error correction to tolerate faults with low overhead.

glossary.name: Financial Modeling
glossary.definition: Applications of quantum algorithms to price options and perform risk analysis more quickly and accurately than classical methods in finance.

glossary.name: Fire Opal Error Suppression Layer
glossary.definition: An error suppression technology layer applied on the Forte system that improves mean circuit fidelity by approximately 12% on benchmark circuits.

glossary.name: Forte Enterprise
glossary.definition: An enterprise-level quantum computing product by IonQ designed for high-demand workloads with dedicated queue access.

glossary.name: Gate Speed
glossary.definition: The speed at which quantum logic gates are executed on qubits, affecting overall quantum computation time.

glossary.name: Goldilocks Zone
glossary.definition: The operational regime where qubit count and gate fidelity increase in lockstep to optimize quantum computer performance.

glossary.name: Google Cloud Marketplace
glossary.definition: Google's cloud platform marketplace providing access to quantum computing services including IonQ's quantum computers.

glossary.name: Hamiltonian Simulation
glossary.definition: A quantum algorithmic technique used in benchmarking to simulate the time evolution of a quantum system governed by a Hamiltonian.

glossary.name: Hardware Optimization
glossary.definition: Improvements made to the quantum computer hardware, such as increasing qubit count and upgrading detection optics, to enhance performance and scale.

glossary.name: Harmony
glossary.definition: IonQ's 11-qubit quantum computing system, support for which will be wound down by the end of 2024 to reallocate engineering capacity.

glossary.name: Ion Trap Chips
glossary.definition: Electrodes and electrical connections built using conventional micro-fabrication technologies that create conditions for ion qubits to be trapped in space.

glossary.name: Iteration Cycle Responsiveness
glossary.definition: The responsiveness of the quantum computing system to support rapid iteration cycles for researchers.

glossary.name: Job Queue Latency
glossary.definition: The time delay experienced by jobs waiting in the queue before execution on a quantum computing system.

glossary.name: Job Queue Performance
glossary.definition: Performance measure of the job queue system, focusing on minimizing wait times for quantum job execution.

glossary.name: Laser Cooling
glossary.definition: A technique using low-power laser beams to cool atomic ions, improving vacuum environment and qubit coherence without degrading qubit properties at room temperature.

glossary.name: Laser Delivery and Control Systems
glossary.definition: Systems developed to implement fully programmable, fully connected quantum gate schemes by delivering and controlling laser beams for qubit manipulation.

glossary.name: Microsoft Azure Quantum
glossary.definition: Microsoft's cloud platform offering access to quantum computing resources including IonQ's quantum computers.

glossary.name: Modular Quantum Architecture
glossary.definition: A quantum computer architecture where individual quantum processing units are connected to form increasingly powerful systems, enabling scalable quantum computing.

glossary.name: Modular Quantum Computers
glossary.definition: Quantum computers small enough to be networked together in a datacenter to scale performance.

glossary.name: Monte Carlo Circuits
glossary.definition: A family of benchmark circuits used in the #AQ repository to evaluate quantum computer performance.

glossary.name: Multi-QPU Protocols
glossary.definition: Specialized protocols used in multi-quantum processing unit environments to optimize performance by managing entanglement generation and multi-qubit gate implementation.

glossary.name: Optimization Problems
glossary.definition: Complex problems in industries such as logistics, pharmaceutical drug design, and climate modeling that can benefit from quantum algorithms to find better approximate solutions faster.

glossary.name: Phase Estimation
glossary.definition: A quantum algorithmic technique used in benchmarking to estimate the phase (eigenvalue) of an eigenvector of a unitary operator.

glossary.name: Photonic Interconnect
glossary.definition: Technology that uses light particles to communicate between qubits while keeping information stored stably on either end of the interconnect, enabling multi-QPU quantum computers.

glossary.name: Q-CTRL Integration Test
glossary.definition: A collaborative integration test between IonQ and Q-CTRL focusing on error suppression and compilation layers, currently in Phase 2 as of July 8, 2024.

glossary.name: Qiskit
glossary.definition: An open-source quantum computing software development framework used to specify quantum circuits.

glossary.name: Quantum Advantage
glossary.definition: The point at which a quantum computer is able to perform a particular computation that exceeds its classical counterpart in speed or reduces its cost to solution.

glossary.name: Quantum Chemistry Simulation
glossary.definition: The simulation of quantum systems such as molecules to improve understanding and accelerate discovery in chemical and pharmaceutical industries.

glossary.name: Quantum Compiler
glossary.definition: IonQ's software tool that compiles quantum circuits, incorporating optimizations to reduce gate counts and improve performance.

glossary.name: Quantum Computing as a Service
glossary.definition: A cloud-based approach that enables broad availability of quantum computing resources and services.

glossary.name: Quantum Fourier Transform
glossary.definition: A quantum algorithmic technique used in benchmarking, involving transformation of quantum states into the frequency domain.

glossary.name: Quantum Logic Gates
glossary.definition: Operations that create entanglement and perform computation between pairs of qubits, implemented via laser beams in trapped ion systems.

glossary.name: Quantum Machine Learning
glossary.definition: The use of quantum computing to develop new machine-learning modalities that can improve or complement classical machine learning techniques.

glossary.name: Quantum Operating System
glossary.definition: Software that manages the quantum computer hardware and maintains system operation, including converting user quantum programs into executable instructions.

glossary.name: Quantum Processing Unit
glossary.definition: A chip that stores qubits and serves as the fundamental processing unit in a quantum computer, potentially containing multiple cores or zones for trapping chains of ions.

glossary.name: Quantum Volume
glossary.definition: A benchmark introduced by IBM to take into account multiple aspects of early quantum computers.

glossary.name: Reconfigurable Multi-Core Quantum Architectures
glossary.definition: Quantum computing architectures enabled by new IonQ trap technology that allow dynamic reconfiguration of multiple quantum cores.

glossary.name: Remote Entanglement Rate
glossary.definition: The speed at which quantum entanglement is generated between remote quantum processing units, measured in events per second.

glossary.name: Room Temperature Operation
glossary.definition: The capability of trapped ion quantum systems to operate at room temperature due to electromagnetic confinement of qubits in vacuum, unlike solid-state qubits requiring cryogenics.

glossary.name: Sharpening
glossary.definition: An error mitigation technique that does not require additional samples but can degrade performance of some circuits.

glossary.name: Shuttling
glossary.definition: The process of moving ions within a quantum processing unit by modifying the electromagnetic fields that form the trap to enable quantum communication between cores.

glossary.name: System Uptime
glossary.definition: The percentage of time a quantum computing platform is operational and available for use.

glossary.name: Trapped Ion Qubits
glossary.definition: Qubits represented by internal states of individual atoms trapped and isolated in a vacuum, confined via electric fields in an ultra-high vacuum environment.

glossary.name: Two-Qubit Gate Fidelity
glossary.definition: The average fidelity of two-qubit gate operations, affecting computational power and error correction overhead.

glossary.name: Typical Quantum Program
glossary.definition: A quantum program whose size (number of fully-connected gate operations) scales with the square of the number of algorithmic qubits.

glossary.name: Ultra-High Vacuum Environment
glossary.definition: A vacuum chamber environment used to keep ion qubits well-isolated from external interference, critical for maintaining qubit coherence.

glossary.name: Zero Noise Extrapolation
glossary.definition: An error mitigation technique that scales exponentially in the number of experimental samples to reduce noise effects.

glossary.name: announcement
glossary.definition: The product or capability is publicly announced.

glossary.name: demonstration
glossary.definition: A working demonstration exists, not yet a product.

glossary.name: early access
glossary.definition: Available to selected customers before general release.

glossary.name: end of support
glossary.definition: Support for the product is ended.

glossary.name: first delivery
glossary.definition: First unit delivered or installed at a customer site.

glossary.name: general availability
glossary.definition: Available to customers as a product or service.

glossary.name: upgrade
glossary.definition: A later generation replaces or extends the product.
